events.fact: GitHub API rate limits for REST API are 5,000 requests per hour for authenticated requests (OAuth apps/Personal access tokens), and 15,000 requests per hour for GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations. Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 per hour.
GitHub GraphQL API rate limit is 5,000 points per hour for standard users and apps, scaling to 10,000 points per hour for Enterprise Cloud.
Composio supports bringing your own GitHub App by configuring its client ID and client secret in the GitHub auth config, though GitHub App installation is a separate step from OAuth credential setup.

events.query: site:docs.github.com "creating an OAuth app" steps developer settings

events.fact: Creating a GitHub OAuth app is self-serve via developer settings (Settings -> Developer settings -> OAuth apps -> New OAuth App). Each user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps. Required fields: Application name, Homepage URL, Authorization callback URL.
GitHub does not require a prior review, approval, or verification process for registering or deploying custom OAuth apps. Apps are immediately live for users upon creation.

GitHub OAuth apps support expiring tokens (opt-in). When enabled, access tokens expire after 8 hours (28,800 seconds) and refresh tokens expire after 6 months of inactivity. Token rotation is enforced on refresh.

GitHub OAuth apps do not have OIDC/OAuth discovery documents at /.well-known/openid-configuration or /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. Authorize endpoint is at https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize and token endpoint is at https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token.

events.query: site:docs.github.com "scopes for OAuth apps" repo user workflow
GitHub OAuth app review verification process required or optional

events.fact: Creating an OAuth app requires an application name, homepage URL, and an authorization callback URL. Users can also configure whether user access tokens expire.

The REST API rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour for authenticated requests (OAuth apps/PATs) and 15,000 requests per hour for GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations. Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 per hour.
Authorizing OAuth apps uses a web flow where users grant permissions. Optional parameters include state, login, and allow_signup. Expiring token flows support refresh tokens valid for 6 months.
Typical agent scopes include repo (full control of private/public repositories), workflow (managing GitHub Actions), and read:user (reading user profile data).
